review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for downstream uses of SigmaHom, Sigma.incl, Sigma.desc (category-level) and Functor.sigma/natTrans.sigma. The only external use is ConnectedComponents.lean, which uses Sigma.incl, Sigma.desc and SigmaHom.mk. Nothing outside this file uses Functor.sigma or natTrans.sigma. I found no loops or competing rules. The simps-generated lemmas (desc_obj, incl_map, natIso_hom, mapId and mapComp hom_app/inv_app) look consistent. I could not run Lean, so I don't know whether simp's reducible unfolding already makes comp_def fire on `≫`, and I don't know the exact shape of the lemmas that simps generates. Both findings are therefore about interface quality, not observed failures.

findings.excerpt: lemma comp_def (i : I) (X Y Z : C i) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : comp (mk f) (mk g) = mk (f ≫ g) :=
findings.problem: The only simp lemma about morphism composition in the sigma category has its left-hand side in terms of the internal helper `SigmaHom.comp`. Users and the other lemmas in this file work with categorical composition `mk f ≫ mk g`, and `SigmaHom.comp` is only the implementation behind `CategoryStruct.comp`. Whether the lemma applies to `≫` depends on simp unfolding the instance reducibly. The orientation and head symbol are not the canonical one. There is also no companion simp lemma for the identity, such as `𝟙 ⟨i, X⟩ = mk (𝟙 X)` (the helper `SigmaHom.id` is likewise not exposed). So `mk`-built morphisms have no stated normal form for `𝟙` and `≫`.
findings.proposed_change: State the simp lemma in the user-facing form: `@[simp] lemma mk_comp_mk ... : mk f ≫ mk g = mk (f ≫ g) := rfl`. Optionally keep `comp_def` unannotated for the helper. Consider adding `@[simp] lemma id_mk (X : C i) : 𝟙 (⟨i, X⟩ : Σ i, C i) = mk (𝟙 X) := rfl` only if it is checked not to fight `Functor.map_id` or `incl_obj`. In that case the direction should be chosen so that `(incl i).map (𝟙 X)` and `𝟙 ((incl i).obj X)` reach one normal form.
findings.benefit: Simp goals about `mk f ≫ mk g` would reduce to `mk (f ≫ g)` without relying on reducible unfolding of the category instance. The simp set would then be phrased in the public `≫` / `𝟙` vocabulary instead of the private helper `comp`.

findings.excerpt: desc fun i => F i ⋙ incl i
findings.problem: `Functor.sigma` and `natTrans.sigma` are plain `def`s with no simp lemmas. Every other construction in the file (`natTrans`, `desc`, `inclDesc`, `descUniq`, `map`, `natIso`, `mapId`, `mapComp`) has `@[simp]` or `@[simps]` lemmas for its components. A term such as `(Functor.sigma F).obj ⟨i, X⟩` is therefore stuck for simp. `Functor.sigma F` is not reducible, so `desc_obj` and `desc_map_mk` do not see through it. The same holds for `(Functor.sigma F).map (SigmaHom.mk f)` and `(natTrans.sigma α).app ⟨i, X⟩`. The expected normal forms are `⟨i, (F i).obj X⟩`, `SigmaHom.mk ((F i).map f)` and `SigmaHom.mk ((α i).app X)`.
findings.proposed_change: Add simp lemmas in the style of `map_obj`, `map_map` and `natTrans_app`. For example: `@[simp] lemma Functor.sigma_obj (F) (i) (X : C i) : (Functor.sigma F).obj ⟨i, X⟩ = ⟨i, (F i).obj X⟩ := rfl`, `@[simp] lemma Functor.sigma_map ... (f : X ⟶ Y) : (Functor.sigma F).map (SigmaHom.mk f) = SigmaHom.mk ((F i).map f) := rfl`, and `@[simp] lemma natTrans.sigma_app (α) (i) (X : C i) : (natTrans.sigma α).app ⟨i, X⟩ = SigmaHom.mk ((α i).app X) := rfl`. Alternatively use `@[simps]` and verify the generated statements.
findings.benefit: Users of the assembled functor and natural transformation get the same simp coverage as the rest of the file. Without it they must `unfold` or `dsimp [Functor.sigma, desc]` and then also handle the `incl_obj` / `Functor.comp_obj` residue by hand.
